title: Complex data analysis with cuplyr
text: Ten thousand transactions one year.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 10000  sales_data <- data.frame(  transaction_id = seq_len(n),  date = as.Date("2023-01-01") + sample(0:364, n, replace = TRUE),  customer_id = sample(1:500, n, replace = TRUE),  product_category = sample(c("Electronics", "Clothing", "Food", "Home", "Sports"),                            n, replace = TRUE),  region = sample(c("North", "South", "East", "West"), n, replace = TRUE),  quantity = sample(1:10, n, replace = TRUE),  unit_price = round(runif(n, 5, 500), 2),  discount_pct = sample(c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20), n, replace = TRUE,                        prob = c(0.5, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05)) )  gpu_sales <- tbl_gpu(sales_data)

title: Complex data analysis with cuplyr
text: Derive revenue, drop small transactions, aggregate category region. Nothing runs collect().
code: revenue_analysis <- gpu_sales |>  mutate(    gross_amount = quantity * unit_price,    discount_amount = gross_amount * discount_pct / 100,    net_revenue = gross_amount - discount_amount  ) |>  filter(net_revenue > 50) |>  group_by(product_category, region) |>  summarise(    total_revenue = sum(net_revenue),    total_transactions = n(),    avg_transaction = mean(net_revenue),    total_quantity = sum(quantity)  ) |>  arrange(desc(total_revenue)) |>  collect() #> `summarise()` has regrouped the output by dropping the last grouping variable. #> Summaries were computed grouped by product_category, region. #> Output is grouped by product_category. #> Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message, or `.groups = "keep"`/`"drop"` to retain/drop every grouping level.  head(revenue_analysis, 10) #> # A tibble: 10 × 6 #> # Groups:   product_category [5] #>    product_category region total_revenue total_transactions avg_transaction #>    <chr>            <chr>          <dbl>              <int>           <dbl> #>  1 Sports           West         720716.                531           1357. #>  2 Food             West         711706.                517           1377. #>  3 Clothing         South        706586.                509           1388. #>  4 Food             East         701067.                514           1364. #>  5 Sports           East         698596.                501           1394. #>  6 Sports           South        691472.                507           1364. #>  7 Electronics      South        683388.                528           1294. #>  8 Clothing         North        664092.                487           1364. #>  9 Electronics      North        663955.                504           1317. #> 10 Home             East         663267.                504           1316. #> # ℹ 1 more variable: total_quantity <int>

title: Complex data analysis with cuplyr

A sample is a batch of calls fenced with gpu_sync(); # gc() runs untimed before every batch. per_call <- function(fn, samples = 15, warmup = 3, target = 0.03) {   for (i in seq_len(warmup)) fn()   gpu_sync(); gc(verbose = FALSE)   t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]; fn(); gpu_sync()   one <- max(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0, 1e-4)   reps <- max(1L, min(500L, as.integer(ceiling(target / one))))   t <- vapply(seq_len(samples), function(i) {     gc(verbose = FALSE)     t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]     for (j in seq_len(reps)) fn()     gpu_sync()     (proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0) / reps   }, numeric(1))   1e3 * median(t) }  # GPU memory one call leaves allocated until R's next gc(), in MB. held_mb <- function(fn) {   gc(verbose = FALSE); gc(verbose = FALSE); gpu_sync()   u0 <- gpu_memory_state()$pool_used_bytes   r <- fn(); gpu_sync()   u1 <- gpu_memory_state()$pool_used_bytes   rm(r)   (u1 - u0) / 1e6 }  pipeline <- function(d) {   d |>     filter(x > 0.1) |>     mutate(z = x * y + w) |>     group_by(g) |>     summarise(m = mean(z), n = n()) |>     arrange(desc(m)) }  n <- 1e6 df <- data.frame(g = sample.int(100L, n, TRUE), x = runif(n), y = runif(n),                  w = rnorm(n)) tb <- tibble::as_tibble(df) eg <- tbl_gpu(df, lazy = FALSE) lz <- tbl_gpu(df, lazy = TRUE)  c(eager = per_call(function() collect(pipeline(eg))),   lazy  = per_call(function() collect(pipeline(lz))),   dplyr = per_call(function() pipeline(tb))) c(eager = held_mb(function() collect(pipeline(eg))),   lazy  = held_mb(function() collect(pipeline(lz))))

title: Resolve the common GPU type for one column across a bind/set operation — resolve_common_col_type
text: Four cases, pinned via oracle-verified dplyr/vctrs behavior: factor (DICTIONARY32): union level sets (-op identical) – vctrs::vec_c(factor, factor)'s contract. Exactly one factor, STRING: decodes STRING (dplyr's factor + character -> character contract). Exactly one factor, anything else (numeric, timestamp, ...): hard incompatibility ($ok = FALSE) – real vctrs::vec_ptype2() refuses . Identical types: -op. numeric ladder (BOOL8 < INT32 < INT64 < FLOAT64, except INT64 (integer64) FLOAT64 common type) timestamp ladder (TIMESTAMP_DAYS < ... < TIMESTAMP_NANOSECONDS): promotes wider member. timestamp cast (Date <-> POSIXct, etc.) native (gpu_cast_column(), src/ops_bind.cpp, handles TIMESTAMP_* targets), ladder native callers. Anything else (e.g. numeric vs. character, factor vs. numeric, numeric vs. timestamp): $ok = FALSE – caller reports verb-specific incompatibility error (sets.R's "xandy compatible." bulleted form vs. bind.R's vctrs-style "combine ..."form, seeabort_bind_rows_incompatible()`).
